messages:
miriam: Kicking off ap-northeast-1 GPU cluster bring-up for the new recommender workload. Target: EKS 1.29, nodepools with g5.2xlarge (A10G) for inference and a smaller spot pool for batch. Need validation checklist + handoff to oncall when green. Questions: CNI choice, ENI/IP planning, driver install, autoscaler config, and cost estimate.

samir: +1. I'll own the infra bits. Quick notes: AWS ENI IPs are the usual gotcha in dense pod-per-node setups. For g5.2xlarge we get ~50 IPs per ENI? we need to calculate max pods per node vs desired GPU pods.

noah: For runtime, prefer BottleRocket or AmazonLinux2 AMI with containerd. Driver install: best to bake an AMI with NVIDIA driver + nvidia-container-toolkit preinstalled. Otherwise user-data is fragile on kernel updates.

anya: Checklist I want before handoff: quota checks (ENI, vCPU, EBS), subnet IPs for pod density, KMS key for secrets, logging sink to our central ES, and an alert runbook for OOM/kubelet evictions. Also confirm private endpoint config for the cluster.

samir: Here's the nodegroup snippet I'm testing with eksctl (simplified):
```yaml
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
metadata:
  name: recommender-apne1
  region: ap-northeast-1
managedNodeGroups:
  - name: gpus-primary
    instanceType: g5.2xlarge
    desiredCapacity: 4
    minSize: 2
    maxSize: 8
    labels: {role: gpu, workload: realtime}
    iam:
      withAddonPolicies: {autoScaler: true}
```
Plan: separate spot group for batch with mixed instances (g5/g4dn) behind the same autoscaler.

miriam: For CNI we discussed two options: amazon-vpc-cni for max performance and native ENI IPs, or Calico (CNI chaining) if we want more flexible networking. Prefer amazon-vpc-cni unless we need network policies immediately.

samir: Agree. If we go amazon-vpc-cni, we must set maxPods correctly. eksctl sets it automatically by instance type but double-check: `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.capacity.pods}'`. Also tag subnets: `kubernetes.io/cluster/recommender-apne1 = shared` for node provisioning.

noah: User-data bootstrap snippet I tested (fallback if we don't bake AMI):
```bash
#!/bin/bash -xe
# install nvidia driver + toolkit (quick, not production hardened)
yum install -y kernel-devel-$(uname -r)
# fetch NVIDIA driver, install
curl -fsSL https://us.archive.ubuntu.com/some-driver.sh | bash
# install nvidia-container-toolkit
apt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
systemctl restart systemd-modules-load
```
Don't use this verbatim — I'm posting for visibility. We want a Packer AMI pipeline.

anya: ENI/IP math: for g5.2xlarge (nv4?) assume 2 ENIs with N IPs each — confirm with AWS table. If we plan 4 GPU pods per node with 1 pod IP each + system pods, plan for ~10-12 pods capacity per node. If you try to cram 40 pods, ENI limits bite us.

samir: Autoscaler plan: cluster-autoscaler with ASG tags + scale-down delay 10m. We'll annotate GPU nodegroups to prefer GPU-scheduled pods: `k8s.amazonaws.com/accelerator: nvidia.com/gpu`. Also enable the TAINT + toleration pattern so non-GPU workloads don't land there.

miriam: Cost estimate rough: g5.2xlarge on demand ~ $1.6/hr (NA numbers as reference) — double-check ap-northeast-1 pricing; plan uses reserved for baseline and spot for burst. Ops: id responsible for pricing confirmation?

samir: I'll run a cost model. Want baseline 4 nodes reserved + up to 8 spot. Also enable our tokenized billing tags: `project:recommender`, `env:prod` for chargeback.

ops-bot: IAM role `eks-reco-node-role` created (arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/eks-reco-node-role).

noah: Validation commands to run post-provision (run as cluster-admin):
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` (confirm instance types + age)
- `kubectl describe node <gpu-node>` (check allocatable pods, labels, taints)
- `kubectl run -it --rm --restart=Never gpu-test --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.7-base --requests='nvidia.com/gpu:1' --limits='nvidia.com/gpu:1' --command -- nvidia-smi`
- `kubectl logs daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n kube-system`
If `nvidia-smi` works inside pod, driver path is good.

anya: Handoff steps for oncall:
1) Ensure alerts exist: NodeNotReady, kubelet_eviction, DiskPressure, GPU-driver-fail.
2) Pager duties for first 72h: Samir + Oncall rotation.
3) Run smoke tests: 3 inference pods hitting model endpoint ~ 50 rps total.
4) Confirm backups of cluster-autoscaler config and ASG policies.

miriam: Assign owners: Samir = infra boot, Noah = runtime/AMI + validation scripts, Anya = runbook & alerts, Miriam = product sign-off + cost. I'll post the final handoff message when all green.

samir: I'll run the eksctl apply tonight in staging and post results here. Expecting subnets + ENI tagging to be the main rework.

miriam: Thank you. If anyone hits quota errors, tag @cloud-ops. We'll do a final dry-run deploy tomorrow 03:00 UTC. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
